newsitem.title: USA: NAST, NACo delegates adopt key muni resolutions.
newsitem.headline: NAST, NACo delegates adopt key muni resolutions.

text.p: Over 3,400 U.S. county representatives on Tuesday called on Congress to delay enacting Internet taxation bills and to work closely with them in any plan to restructure the U.S. electric power industry.

The final vote by delegates to the National Association of Counties' (NACo) 62nd annual conference came one day after state treasurers, meeting in San Diego, adopted a separate round of resolutions on issues ranging from private activity bond volume caps to the so-called two percent deminimis rule.
County delegates urged Congress not to move forward with House and Senate bills seeking a moratorium on state and local taxes that target the Internet until the potential impacts can be studied.
Delegates worry that the bills will cut deep into state and local revenues, they said..
Another resolution adopted Tuesday warns that any national plan to restructure the nation's electric utility industry must include counties as "partners."

"State and local government leaders must be partners in any national restructuring plan," says the resolution, which sets out 13 principles concerning transition periods, rights of way, and other issues.

In San Diego, meanwhile, the National Association of State Treasurers (NAST) voted to urge Congress and the White House to support bills to increase per capita limits and statewide volume caps on the use of private activity bonds.
Limits should be indexed to account for inflation and states should be permitted to carry forward any private activity bond authority that is unused in the year it arises, treasurers said.
Treasurers also urged Congress and the President to reject legislation that would repeal the so-called two-percent de minimis.
